Markers let breeders estimate relatedness, plan matings, trace parentage and map quantitative trait loci. Genomic selection predicts breeding values from thousands of markers at once.

sections.heading: Inbreeding and conservation
sections.text:
Inbreeding raises homozygosity and causes inbreeding depression: slower growth, lower survival, more deformity. Effective population size, Ne, measures how many breeders actually contribute. With Nm males and Nf females, Ne = 4NmNf ÷ (Nm + Nf), and inbreeding rises by about 1 ÷ (2Ne) per generation. A common guideline is Ne of at least 50, keeping inbreeding near 1% per generation.

Example: 50 males and 50 females give Ne = 4 × 50 × 50 ÷ 100 = 100, so ΔF = 1 ÷ 200 = 0.005, or 0.5%.

Conserving aquatic genetic resources means keeping wild populations, local strains and cryopreserved material, with recorded origins.

keyPoints: Narrow-sense heritability is h² = V_A ÷ V_P, and it applies only to the population and environment measured.
Response to selection per generation is R = h²S, where S is the selection differential.
Crossbreeding and hybridisation can give heterosis, but hybrids may be sterile or have skewed sex ratios.
DNA markers such as microsatellites and SNPs are used for parentage, relatedness and genomic selection.
Effective population size is Ne = 4NmNf ÷ (Nm + Nf), and inbreeding rises by about 1 ÷ (2Ne) per generation.
Keep Ne at 50 or more, avoid mating close relatives, and conserve wild and local strains.

en.title: Advanced Aquaculture Systems and Biotechnology
en.short: RAS, biofloc, IMTA, water treatment and biotech for fish health, feed and reproduction.

sections.heading: Recirculating systems
sections.text: A recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) keeps fish in tanks and reuses most water. Water treatment engineering uses mechanical filters for solids, a biofilter where nitrifying bacteria convert toxic ammonia to nitrite and then nitrate, gas exchange for oxygen and carbon dioxide, and often disinfection and temperature control. RAS gives high stocking density, biosecurity and low land and water use. Costs are high: capital, energy for pumps and oxygen, and skilled monitoring. Environmental limits include concentrated sludge and nitrate waste, energy demand and need for backup power.

sections.heading: Biofloc and IMTA
sections.text: Biofloc is a system where a microbial community, mainly bacteria, grows in the water and is eaten by fish or shrimp. It needs strong aeration and a carbon source to raise the carbon to nitrogen (C:N) ratio, and it uses little water exchange. Integrated multi-trophic aquaculture (IMTA) farms fed species with extractive species such as seaweed and filter feeders, so waste nutrients become food. Biofloc can lower feed cost but uses energy and produces sludge. IMTA can improve nutrient use but needs compatible species, space and careful ratios.

sections.heading: Biotechnology tools
sections.text: In disease diagnosis, PCR and qPCR detect pathogen DNA or RNA, ELISA detects antibodies or antigens, and portable tests allow farm-level screening. In nutrition, enzymes, probiotics and single-cell proteins improve feed use and reduce fishmeal dependence. In reproduction, hormones such as GnRH analogues induce spawning, and cryopreservation stores sperm. These tools raise performance but need laboratories, trained staff and quality control.

sections.heading: Comparison and case
sections.text: A small Nigerian farm with scarce land might choose RAS for tilapia fingerlings because it controls water and disease, but it must budget for electricity and a backup generator. A coastal shrimp farm with ponds may use biofloc to cut water exchange, or IMTA with seaweed where site and species suit. No system is always best: RAS has high control and high cost, biofloc medium cost and high aeration, IMTA lower input cost but site-dependent. Check local rules and current prices.

keyPoints: RAS reuses water through solids removal, nitrification, gas exchange and disinfection.
Biofloc uses a microbial community, aeration and a carbon source to recycle nutrients and reduce water exchange.
IMTA pairs fed species with extractive species to turn waste nutrients into products.
PCR and ELISA are core tools for rapid pathogen diagnosis; probiotics and enzymes support nutrition; hormones and cryopreservation support reproduction.
RAS has high control and high energy cost; biofloc needs aeration; IMTA is site and species dependent.
Compare systems on capital, energy, skilled labour, water use and waste before choosing.

en.title: Advanced Research Design and the Dissertation
en.short: Sampling, design, multivariate and spatial analysis, ethics, funding and dissertation planning.

sections.heading: Sampling and design
sections.text: Advanced sampling starts with a sampling frame, the list from which units are drawn. Probability methods such as simple random, stratified, cluster and multistage sampling allow design-based estimates with known inclusion probabilities. Sample size depends on variance, effect size, precision and expected nonresponse. Experimental design uses randomisation, replication and blocking to separate treatment effects from nuisance variation. Survey design covers questionnaire wording, mode, piloting and nonresponse bias. For a survey proportion, n = z²p(1−p) ÷ e². With z = 1.96, p = 0.5 and e = 0.05, n = 384.16, so 385.

sections.heading: Multivariate and spatial analysis
sections.text: Multivariate methods analyse many variables together. Principal component analysis reduces correlated measurements to a few axes; ordination and cluster analysis describe community patterns; regression models test covariates. Geospatial analysis joins observations to coordinates, maps hotspots and tests spatial autocorrelation, the tendency of nearby sites to be similar. Tools such as R, Python and GIS make work reproducible through scripts, version control and documented workflows. Check model assumptions and validate predictions.

sections.heading: Ethics and funding
sections.text: Research ethics covers permits, animal welfare, informed consent, data protection, plagiarism and authorship. Fisheries fieldwork may affect protected species or local communities, so follow national rules and institutional ethics committees. A funding proposal states the problem, objectives, methods, budget, timeline, ethics and outputs, and shows feasibility. Keep promises to funders and participants.

sections.heading: Writing and dissertation
sections.text: Scientific writing uses a clear structure, usually IMRaD: Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Tie every claim to evidence and report uncertainty. Plan the dissertation with a proposal, supervisor meetings, timeline, pilot study, data management plan and risk log. Execute in stages: literature review, fieldwork, analysis, writing, revision and defence. Keep raw data and code so others can check the work.

keyPoints: Probability sampling gives known inclusion probabilities; sample size depends on variance, precision and nonresponse.
For a proportion, n = z²p(1−p) ÷ e²; with z = 1.96, p = 0.5 and e = 0.05, n = 385.
Randomisation, replication and blocking protect experiments from confounding.
Multivariate and geospatial methods need assumption checks and reproducible scripts.
Ethics approval, permits, consent and data protection come before fieldwork.
A dissertation is managed as a project with a proposal, timeline, pilot, data plan and staged writing.
